newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo says H1 profits, sales lower.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo says H1 profits, sales lower.

text.p: British drugs group Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Thursday profits slipped back slightly in the first half of the year, reined in by a strong pound.

Pre-tax profit fell 2.2 percent to 1.517 billion stg ($2.5 billion) from 1.551 billion, while sales were 1.9 percent lower at 4.109 billion stg. However, at constant exchange rates, sales were up eight percent, while operating profit rose six percent.

Analysts had been expecting pre-tax profit of between 1.480 and 1.550 billion pounds. The dividend was maintained at 15.0 pence, to be repaid entirely as a foreign income dividend, reflecting the company's stated goal of rebalancing the interim and final dividends.

Sales of anti-ulcer drug Zantac, which is about to face generic competition in the U.S, were down 12 percent and accounted for 20 percent of total sales, while sales of all other products rose by 14 percent.
Sales of newer products launched since 1990 jumped 50 percent to 1.3 billion stg.

Chairman and chief executive Sir Richard Sykes said the company was on track to achieve its prediction of flat sales and earnings growth in 1997 and 1998 as Zantac declined, before moving back into double digit growth in 1999.
The company plans a 10-month trading update in November. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
